records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: The paper explicitly establishes an 8-bank organization for the register components.

records.claim: num_logical_registers default is 65.
records.why: Table 3 explicitly sizes the register tables across 65 logical registers.

records.claim: decay_threshold default is 256 decoded instructions.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: The paper directly specifies invalidating digests after 256 subsequent decoded instructions.

records.claim: digest_width default is 12 bits.
records.quote: RUNLTS generates a 12-bit digest from each 64-bit register value, with the format depending on the register type.
records.why: The paper explicitly defines the register digest width as 12 bits.

records.claim: wt_weight_width default is 6 bits.
records.why: Table 3 gives the weight width of prediction table WT as 6 bits.

records.claim: useful_multiplier default is 2.5.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) explicitly labels the bank output multiplier stage as x0 or x2.5.

records.claim: ut_entries_per_table default is 8.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) and Table 3 specify 8 entries per usefulness table.

records.claim: test_int_digest_xor_folding produces 0xB51 for value 0x2A by XOR folding trailing zeros count, leading zeros count shifted by 3, and value LSBs shifted by 6.
records.quote: For integer registers, the digest encodes the count of leading zeros (or ones), the count of trailing zeros (or ones), and the six least significant bits, effectively capturing characteristics of addresses and round numbers.
records.why: Figure 6(a) defines the three 6-bit fields overlapping with XOR at bit offsets 0, 3, and 6, which yields 0x01 ^ (0x3A << 3) ^ (0x2A << 6) = 0xB51.

records.claim: test_flag_digest_replication produces 0xBBB for flag 0xB by replicating the 4-bit value three times across the 12-bit digest.
records.quote: For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: The paper specifies 3-way replication of the 4 flag bits, producing 0b101110111011 = 0xBBB.

records.claim: test_fp32_digest_extraction extracts Value[31:26] positioned at digest bits [8:3].
records.quote: For floating-point registers, we inspect the most significant bits to classify the format and then extract the sign bit along with the most significant bits of the exponent.
records.why: Figure 6(b) specifies extracting Value[31:26] into digest bits [8:3] for FP32.

records.claim: test_register_decay_invalidation invalidates an entry after exactly 256 subsequent decoded instructions.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: The paper explicitly states that digests are invalidated after 256 subsequent decoded instructions.

records.claim: test_bank_usefulness_argmax_selection selects the register with maximum usefulness in the bank and scales WT sum by 2.5 when usefulness > 0.
records.quote: Unlike the existing components, this component picks the digest of the most useful register among those available and forwards it to the second table.
records.why: Argmax selection forwards the most useful register to WT, and positive usefulness enables the 2.5x multiplier stage shown in Figure 5(c).

records.claim: test_bank_negative_usefulness_suppression suppresses bank output to 0 via x0 multiplier when best usefulness is negative or zero.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) specifies that bank contribution is scaled by x0 when the bank's usefulness is non-positive.

records.claim: test_post_misprediction_value_availability makes digests of instructions completing before pipeline flush available to subsequent branch predictions.
records.quote: However, we found that by the time a branch resolves and its misprediction is revealed, many in-flight instructions have already finished execution, thereby enlarging the set of values visible to the predictor when it restarts, and this fact can be exploited.
records.why: The paper explicitly notes that completed in-flight producer values are retained across flush and visible upon restart.

records.claim: predict_sr iterates over 8 banks, finds available valid registers, and sums combined usefulness from UT0, UT1, and UT2.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2". Their outputs go to a Sigma producing "9 regs useful (skewed)".
records.why: Figure 5(c) shows summing outputs of UT0, UT1, UT2 across banks, and subscripting by register r ranges over the same logical register domain [0, 64] as chosen_reg in update, refuting the inconsistent index warning.

records.claim: predict_sr selects the register with highest usefulness (argmax) and indexes WT0, WT1, WT2 using hash functions h0, h1, h2 of PC and register digest.
records.quote: Selected digest plus PC form the input labelled "PC + reg. digest", hashed into "h0", "h1", "h2". Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1", "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) shows argmax selecting the digest for hashing into WT0, WT1, WT2; h0, h1, h2 have identical domains in predict and update, refuting the inconsistent index warning.

records.claim: predict_sr applies a 2.5x multiplier to the WT weight sum when best usefulness is positive, and 0x multiplier otherwise, summing over all 8 banks to produce sR_sum.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) shows the per-bank WT sum routed through the x0/x2.5 multiplier into the final adder producing sR, and refutes undefined helper findings since length is a host list primitive and 'as' is parsed from an explanatory code comment.
